A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Phantom framework. Text, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A-D are readable and matchable. The extra bibliography page in v3 shifts the appendix without removing material.

before.justification: v1 reports original Phantom benchmark results, the alternative-encoder ablation in Table 6, and force-conditioned generation examples in Appendix D and Figure 6.

after.justification: v3 retains these original benchmark results, encoder ablation, and force-conditioned generation examples, including the appendix evidence.

M1.justification: Sections 4.1-4.2 retain the same Wan2.2/V-JEPA2 dual-branch architecture, cross-attention, joint flow-matching objectives, and cyclic loss weighting. Appendix D's force-conditioning adaptation is also unchanged. The new lightweight-branch description does not establish a procedural change.

E1.justification: Both versions use OpenVidHD-0.4M, VideoPhy, VideoPhy-2, Physics-IQ, VBench-2, and the Force-Prompting application. Text, image, multi-frame, and local point-force conditioning coverage remains unchanged.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in the corresponding tables and qualitative comparisons, including Figures 4-5. Newly cited REPA, ReDi, and Video-JAM appear in related work, not as newly evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: Section 5 and Appendix A retain the same training budget, resolution, conditioning procedures, prompt variants, evaluators, and scoring thresholds. Appendix D retains the same force-input processing and 1.1K-step fine-tuning protocol.

E4.justification: Table 6 retains the same V-JEPA2 versus VideoMAEv2 ablation. The qualitative case comparisons and force-control demonstrations are unchanged; no robustness, sensitivity, or error analysis is added or removed.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. Statistical and uncertainty reporting practices remain unchanged.

E6.justification: Tables 1-6 and the qualitative examples retain their results. For example, Phantom's VideoPhy PC remains 37.9, VideoPhy-2 PC remains 71.74, Physics-IQ single/multi-frame scores remain 29.59/27.53, and VBench-2 total remains 51.84.

T1.justification: Equations 1-9, including the flow-matching formulation, joint conditional distribution, attention definitions, and training objectives, are unchanged. No formal assumptions, derivations, theorems, or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: Section 6 removes the explicit assertion that the design provides a stronger internal understanding of evolving physical processes, retaining claims about visual fidelity and physical plausibility. This softening is confined to the conclusion; the abstract, introduction, and contribution list retain their scope.

C2.justification: Section 2 newly presents the frozen visual backbone and lightweight physics branch as enabling physics-aware reasoning at lower cost. This adds a qualitative efficiency rationale without cost measurements. Existing interpretations of physical consistency, reduced diversity, and force-control behavior remain unchanged.

D1.justification: The acknowledgments newly disclose use of NCSA Delta GPUs through two ACCESS allocations. Appendix A retains the same four-H200 specification and hyperparameters, so this is additional resource documentation rather than evidence of a changed experimental setup. Access links remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds REPA, ReDi, and Video-JAM, explaining their representation-alignment, joint-feature, and motion-supervision approaches and contrasting them with Phantom. An ACCESS infrastructure reference is also added. Existing cited works and the broader research positioning are retained.

P1.justification: Related work is locally rewritten and expanded, the VPhysics-aware heading typo is corrected, the conclusion is shortened, and acknowledgments are extended. The overall section structure and appendix organization remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Figures 1-6 and Tables 1-6 retain their visual content and structure. Revised prose causes local reflow, and the expanded acknowledgments and references occupy an additional bibliography page, shifting the unchanged appendix from PDF pages 11-15 to 12-16.

improvement.justification: v3 improves contextualization by explicitly distinguishing Phantom from REPA, ReDi, and Video-JAM, and provides fuller computing-resource attribution. These are limited gains in positioning and documentation. The empirical evidence is unchanged, and the newly stated lower-cost advantage remains unquantified.
